_about: Verified rules for the company pass. Every name here is a companies.name as it stood in the 2026-09-24 snapshot; the pipeline fails loudly if one no longer resolves (or resolves to a renamed row, by its new name). Rules are applied on top of the automatic ones: a work domain (reduced to the domain its owner registers) belongs to exactly one company, so rows sharing one are merged.

_typo_domains_about: Misspelled mail domains. The address is rewritten to the correct domain (local part untouched), filed under the company that owns it, and marked valid. _ids._about: companies.id of every name above, pinned from the 2026-09-24 snapshot. Rules resolve through these ids, so a later rename ("Yahoo Inc" -> "Yahoo") can't redirect a rule meant for another row (the old "Yahoo" pseudo-company). New rules may omit their ids.

personal_contacts.why: Owner's instruction (2026-09-25): personal addresses (gmail, yahoo, outlook…) aren't wanted in the catalog.
personal_contacts.keep_if_sent: A contact with send history is held for an explicit decision: deleting it cascades to its mail_sends, and the send record is what prevents a duplicate cold mail if it's re-imported.

dead_domains._about: Mail hosts that provably cannot receive email, checked 2026-09-25 on two resolvers (1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8). Contacts on them are deleted (held if they have sends) and the hosts are kept out of companies.domains. Website-only hosts (no MX but an A record) are NOT here: port 25 is blocked from the checking machine, so their bounce couldn't be proven.
